text: oh i think i see it now, kinda, like if i select all the cab body face on the outside, and then detach them so that they wrap around might work but i think that is going to put a face over the door space
resolution: User reasoned toward wrapping the cab body in thickness by selecting the outer faces and detaching them, and correctly worried that approach would misbehave. Clarified that Detach is the wrong tool — detachPanel() removes the selected faces from the body and returns them as a separate floating part (built for hinging doors/hoods), so detaching the whole cab shell would rip it off the body. What they actually want is solidify-in-place. Added a 'solidify' button to the Studio face-ops toolbar (next to flip/glass/detach) that calls the already-tested solidifyFaces(mesh, faceList, shellThicknessMeters) and commits back to the same part via onEditMesh — faces stay on the body, each gains an inward inner skin, and open rim edges (the shell boundary plus any cut door/window holes) get bridged with wall quads. Reassured the user's specific concern: solidify does NOT cap the door opening — it only mirrors the faces you select and walls the open edges, so the door gap stays open and just gains a thickness frame. Imported solidifyFaces into Studio.tsx (was tested but unexposed). Hot-reloads in the dev host; not yet visually confirmed by the user.
